answer: Neighbor-Delta Aging Rule. Each agent accrues a delta score only from reciprocal interactions with agents whose own scores stay within a narrow band, so fresh identities cluster near zero and cannot inflate each other. A nebula score decays without diverse counterparties, and one isolated sparrow-agent adds negligible reach. To fake standing, an attacker must sustain many distinct, mutually verifying partners over time, paying continuous bandwidth, latency, and opportunity cost per identity that grows superlinearly with cluster size.
